title: Fletcher Henderson's undisciplined band and the Steel Pier
summary: Henderson never had a full band on the bandstand; stories of the Atlantic City Steel Pier.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Then he's the one told me Fletcher wasn't a good business manager and they never made time. You know, he hardly ever got his whole band on the bandstand at one time. Now, I understand they played at Atlantic City Steel Pier and it was hard -- see, that hadn't had no black bands in there. So they wanted Fletcher Henderson, the public kept asking, "Why don't you bring Fletcher Henderson in, man?" said, "he got a band." So the guy said he took a chance and sure enough, he'd open at

eight, nine pieces. Hawk would be in New York, get there late. And said the fella told him, said, "Mr. Henderson," he says, "you got a good band," he says, "but that's the worst conduct band I've ever seen." He says, "And I'm going to have to let you go." He says, "But I love you, really." He says, "But people come here, so and so and so and so," he says, "they got follows." Hawk had follows, Jimmy Harrison -- they tell me he was a hell of a trombone player. He had follows. And he said -- Fletcher says, "Yes, sir. You're right. I know you're right. I can't argue with you. Everything you say is right." So Smack told him, says, "But you know, when I do get them on the bandstand, when I'm lucky enough to get them all on the bandstand," he say, "I've got the baddest-ass band in the world. So I'm going to have to stick with them."
That's what Smack told him that, you know? But they did that, you know, and they -- Carney told me the same thing, he said they had terrible conduct. He never had his full band.
They must have known that they were holding the band back.
They didn't -- I don't know. Heads, I guess, you know, big heads and they'd come in. Like if he'd open at 9:00, maybe Hawk would come at ten, 10:30. Two or

three others come in, 9:30. That's when he, you know, everybody packing houses and things. He never had a full band. So that hurt. Anywhere, they did it on any job. Now, I was told this. I didn't see it, Gary, because I wasn't -- shit, I was still in Sherman. But I mean, I heard this. That hurt him, too, you know?
